slides.title: 5 bug and pest myths that waste your money

slides.myth: Plug-in ultrasonic repellers drive out mice and bugs.
slides.fact: The FTC has warned sellers to back that up with real science. Its past cases said mice just get used to the sound, and the devices don't control insects.
slides.source: FTC, via Iowa State University Extension

slides.myth: A bug zapper keeps mosquitoes away.
slides.fact: In a University of Delaware study, only 31 of 13,789 insects zapped were biting flies like mosquitoes. Most of the rest were harmless bugs.

slides.myth: Cheese is the best bait for a mouse trap.
slides.fact: Extension experts put peanut butter first. Use just a small smear. Cheese and fruit are backups.
slides.source: Univ. of Missouri and Utah State Univ. Extension

slides.myth: Daddy longlegs are super venomous, their fangs are just too short.
slides.fact: Harvestmen, the round-bodied ones, aren't even spiders and have no venom glands. Cellar spiders share the nickname, and there's no proof they're the most venomous.

slides.myth: Mothballs in the yard keep snakes away.
slides.fact: Mothballs are pesticides. Using them outdoors goes against the label, which is illegal, and they aren't a proven snake repellent.
slides.source: Florida Dept. of Agriculture, UF/IFAS Extension

slides.title: Which one did you believe?
slides.cta: Follow for the real reason behind everyday stuff
